Definition: Integration of farmer registries, agricultural input vouchers, land registrations, extension services data
Comments: No documented evidence of farmer registry or agricultural data integration into Egypt's G2G data exchange platform. AI in agriculture is mentioned in national AI strategy as future goal.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original cited source (trade.gov ICT guide) does not discuss agriculture at all and is not a relevant citation for this variable. Verified via alternative sources: Egypt operates several digitised agricultural tools — a Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation (MALR) smart-card system (since 2016) linking farmers to fertiliser/pesticide/seed quotas, the Hudhud AI pest-identification app (2021), and the GeoAgro-Misr climate-advisory platform developed with ICARDA/CGIAR — but these operate as standalone sectoral systems. MCIT's own description of the Digital Egypt government-to-government (G2G) data exchange lists the services it currently links (civil status, social insurance, tax, courts, commercial registration, land/vehicle registry) and agriculture is not among them. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (Not integrated): this is a positive finding of non-integration rather than an absence of information, supported by three independent, current sources. Not ambiguous enough to warrant human review.
revised_comments: Egypt operates several digitised agricultural tools, including a Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation (MALR) smart-card system linking farmers to fertiliser, pesticide and seed quotas, the Hudhud AI pest-identification app, and the GeoAgro-Misr climate-advisory platform developed with ICARDA and the CGIAR system. These remain standalone sectoral systems. The national Digital Egypt government-to-government (G2G) data exchange, coordinated by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, currently links civil status, social insurance, tax, courts, commercial registration and land/vehicle registry data, but does not yet include agricultural registries or input-voucher data.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: Limited public disclosure on data exchange operations. Digital Egypt portal statistics are published (8 million users, 45 million transactions). However, no public dashboard or operational transparency for the G2G data exchange system specifically. Annual reporting exists on sector performance.

revision_notes: Second original source (sis.gov.eg) returns HTTP 403 and could not be verified — dead link. First source (masaar.net) covers Egypt's e-government performance generally via the UN EGDI ranking (95th of 193 countries, 2024) but does not address data-exchange-specific transparency, dashboards or inter-agency data-sharing agreements. Fresh searching found MCIT publishes roughly annual statistical press releases on Digital Egypt platform usage (210 services, 10.7 million users, 25m+ requests in 2025) — this is service-uptake reporting, not disclosure of the exchange's governance or data-sharing agreements. Egypt adopted a national Open Data Policy in August 2025 (transitional framework pending a data governance law), which improves general public-data accessibility but does not specifically cover the G2G exchange's operations or agreements. No public dashboard or report on data-exchange governance was found. Score of 2 (Low – Limited Disclosure) confirmed unchanged; the Value Name/scale-label mismatch flagged by redteam is cosmetic only and does not affect the substantive score.
revised_comments: Egypt discloses only limited information specifically about its government-to-government data exchange. The Ministry of Communications and Information Technology publishes periodic statistics on Digital Egypt platform usage (services offered, user numbers, transaction volumes), but these describe front-end service uptake rather than the exchange's governance or inter-agency data-sharing agreements. Egypt's UN E-Government Development Index ranking (95th of 193 countries in 2024) reflects service delivery rather than data-exchange transparency specifically. A national Open Data Policy was adopted in August 2025 as a transitional framework pending a data governance law, improving general public-data accessibility, but it does not extend to disclosure of the data exchange's operational or governance arrangements. No public dashboard or annual report on inter-agency data-sharing agreements was identified.
